## What it is

The steps, by role, for requesting, approving, creating, changing, disabling, removing and reviewing system accounts, with the inputs, outputs and record each step leaves, that carry out the access control policy's account management requirements (SP 800-53 AC-2), separation of duties (AC-5) and the disabling of access when employment ends (PS-4).

## Preview (annotated)

:::note[Guidance]
The Access Control policy's AC-2 statements say what must happen to accounts and who is accountable; this procedure says how, step by step. The AC-2 clause sets AC-2f's "policy, procedures, prerequisites and criteria" to the policy and this procedure, so an assessor reads the two together and then tests the records this procedure says each step leaves. NIST's AC-1 discussion warns that restating controls is not a procedure: fill in the tools, queues and time limits you actually use, and delete nothing an assessor will ask about. The typical values are copied from the Access Control policy's AC-2, AC-2(2), AC-2(3), AC-2(13), AC-5 and AC-6(7) clauses, and the departure time in 5.5 from the Personnel Security policy's PS-4 clause; keep them in step. One procedure can serve every system that uses the organization's identity provider. A system with its own application accounts adds a system-specific section 3 and notes any step it does differently.
:::

### 1. Purpose and scope

This procedure carries out the account management requirements of the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span> Access Control Policy (AC-2). It applies to every account on every system in the system inventory: user, privileged, service, temporary and emergency accounts, in the identity provider, in operating systems and databases, in applications, and in cloud management consoles.

Accounts are managed through <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: automated mechanisms used to support the management of system accounts <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the organization's identity provider and its provisioning workflows</span></span> wherever the system supports it (AC-2(1)). Where it does not, the account manager follows the same steps by hand and records them in the same places.

### 2. Roles

| Role | Responsibilities in this procedure |
| --- | --- |
| Requester | Asks for an account or a change of access, for their own use or for someone they supervise |
| <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Supervisor</span> | Confirms the user's need for access, approves requests, and reports when access is no longer needed or the user's duties change |
| <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> | Decides the system's account types and roles, approves privileged access, assigns account managers, and runs the access review |
| <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: data owner, where different from the system owner</span> | Approves access to the information they own, where the system security plan names one |
| <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> | Checks prerequisites, creates, changes, disables and removes accounts, and keeps the records |
| <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Human resources office</span> | Reports hires, transfers and departures, and starts the [onboarding, transfer and termination checklist](/templates/forms/onboarding-transfer-and-termination-checklist/) |
| <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Security operations team</span> | Monitors account use and reports atypical use |
| <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> | Sets the conditions for access to personally identifiable information, with the system owner |

The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> records the account managers assigned to each system in the system security plan (AC-2b).

### 3. Account types

The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> completes this table for each system, and the account manager creates only the types it allows (AC-2a).

| Account type | Allowed? | Owner | Approval | Ends or is reviewed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Individual user | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: yes or no</span> | The user | <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles required to approve requests to create accounts <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the user's supervisor, plus the system owner or data owner for privileged roles</span></span> | Access review; disabled when no longer required |
| Privileged (administrator) | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: yes or no</span> | The administrator, as a separate account from their user account (AC-6(2)) | Supervisor and system owner | Access review; privileges reviewed <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which to review the privileges assigned to roles or classes of users <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: quarterly for privileged roles and at least annually for all other roles</span></span> |
| Service or system (non-interactive) | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: yes or no</span> | A named person who answers for it | System owner | Access review; disabled when the service it runs is retired |
| Temporary | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: yes or no</span> | The user, with the sponsor named on the request | As for an individual user | Automatically disabled at the approved end date (AC-2(2)) |
| Emergency ("break glass") | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: yes or no</span> | The system owner | System owner, after use | Automatically disabled after the period in step 4.3 (AC-2(2)) |
| Account of last resort | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: yes or no</span> | The system owner | System owner | Access review; credentials held under dual control |
| Shared or group | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: typical: prohibited unless the system owner approves an exception</span> | A named person who answers for it | System owner, as an exception | Authenticators changed whenever a member leaves (step 7) |
| Guest or anonymous | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: typical: prohibited, except on systems designed for public access</span> | Not applicable | Not applicable | Not applicable |

For each account, the account manager records the authorized user, group and role membership, access authorizations and <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: attributes (as required) for each account <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: an expiration date for temporary accounts, and time-of-day or location restrictions where the system supports them</span></span> (AC-2d).

:::note[Guidance]
NIST's AC-2 discussion lists individual, shared, group, system, guest, anonymous, emergency, developer, temporary and service accounts as examples, and names shared, group, emergency, anonymous, temporary and guest accounts as types organizations may prohibit because of their risk. It also separates emergency accounts, which may bypass the normal authorization steps in a crisis and are short-lived, from accounts of last resort, such as local logon accounts used when network resources are unavailable, which stay available and are not subject to automatic disabling. Record any account of last resort here so the inactivity rule in step 5 does not disable it, and the access review still covers it.
:::

### 4. Prerequisites, criteria and separation of duties

Group and role membership is granted only after <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: prerequisites and criteria for group and role membership <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: a completed access request, a signed access agreement and completed security awareness training</span></span> (AC-2c). Access is authorized only on a valid access authorization, the intended system usage and the conditions the system owner sets for the role (AC-2i). Where an account will reach personally identifiable information, the conditions for that role are set with the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span>.

The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> identifies and documents these duties of individuals that require separation: <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: duties of individuals requiring separation <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: requesting and approving access; developing and deploying code to production; administering a system and reviewing its audit logs</span></span> (AC-5a). They are held by different people, and the system's roles are designed so no single account holds both sides (AC-5b):

| Duty | Separated from | How the system enforces it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Requesting access | Approving the same access | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: for example the request tool blocks self-approval</span> |
| Approving access | Granting it in the system | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: for example account managers cannot approve; approvers have no administrative role</span> |
| Administering the system | Reviewing or deleting its audit logs | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: for example logs sent to a platform administrators cannot change</span> |
| Developing code | Deploying it to production | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: for example the pipeline requires an approving review by someone other than the author</span> |
| <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: other duty the system owner names</span> | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: duty</span> | <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: how</span> |

### 5. Procedures

Each step names the role that performs it, what it starts from, what it produces, and the record it leaves. The records are the evidence an assessor samples.

#### 5.1 Request and approve an account or a change of access

| # | Role | Action | Inputs | Outputs | Record |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Requester | Submit an [access request](/templates/forms/access-request-form/) naming the user, system, account type, roles and the business need; for a temporary account, the end date | Need for access | Submitted request | Access request, with its date |
| 2 | <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> | Check the prerequisites in section 4 are met: <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: prerequisites and criteria for group and role membership <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: a completed access request, a signed access agreement and completed security awareness training</span></span> | Request; access agreement register; training records | Request ready for approval, or returned with what is missing | Prerequisite check on the request |
| 3 | <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> | Check the requested roles against section 4 and the user's other roles for separation of duties conflicts | Request; the user's current roles | Conflicts listed, or none | Conflict check on the request |
| 4 | <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles required to approve requests to create accounts <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the user's supervisor, plus the system owner or data owner for privileged roles</span></span> | Approve or reject each role requested. The approver is not the requester, and approves no more than the duties need (AC-6) | Request; conflict check | Approved or rejected request | Approver name and date on the request |
